name: Phenytoin
drug_class: Hydantoin anticonvulsant; voltage-gated sodium channel blocker
route_note: Oral capsules, chewable tablets and suspension; IV for status epilepticus (IM absorption is erratic). Fosphenytoin is a water-soluble IV/IM prodrug.
targets: Voltage-gated sodium channels (SCN1A, SCN2A, SCN8A and others)
originator: Parke-Davis (clinical introduction); first synthesised by Heinrich Biltz

discovery.by: H. Houston Merritt and Tracy Putnam
discovery.note: Identified by screening compounds in an electroshock seizure model in cats; Biltz had synthesised the molecule in 1908.

tagline: Pioneering non-sedating anticonvulsant with famously non-linear kinetics
summary: Phenytoin, introduced in 1938, was the first anticonvulsant shown to control seizures without heavy sedation. It remains widely used for focal and tonic-clonic seizures and status epilepticus, although its saturable metabolism, interactions and long-term adverse effects demand monitoring.
mechanism: Phenytoin binds voltage-gated sodium channels preferentially in their inactivated state, slowing recovery from inactivation. This use-dependent block limits sustained high-frequency repetitive firing of neurons, preventing the spread of seizure activity, while sparing normal low-frequency activity.
It also has class IB antiarrhythmic properties, which explain cardiovascular toxicity when given rapidly intravenously.
uses: Status epilepticus and seizure prophylaxis in neurosurgery (IV)

history.title: Anticonvulsant discovery
history.detail: Merritt and Putnam report its anticonvulsant activity; Parke-Davis markets it as Dilantin.

history.title: Antiarrhythmic use
history.detail: Phenytoin's cardiac sodium-channel effects lead to use for digitalis-induced arrhythmias.

history.title: Fosphenytoin
history.detail: The FDA approves fosphenytoin (Cerebyx), a prodrug with less infusion-site toxicity.

history.title: HLA-B*1502 warning
history.detail: FDA labelling notes an association between HLA-B*15:02 and Stevens-Johnson syndrome/TEN in people of Asian ancestry.

history.title: Pharmacogenomic guideline
history.detail: CPIC publishes a guideline on CYP2C9 and HLA-B genotypes and phenytoin dosing.

pk.half_life: about 22 hours on average (7–42 h), concentration-dependent
pk.metabolism: hepatic, CYP2C9 and CYP2C19; saturable (Michaelis–Menten) kinetics

serious: Purple glove syndrome with IV use
safety.boxed_warning: Cardiovascular risk with rapid intravenous infusion (hypotension and arrhythmias); IV rate must not exceed labelled limits.

facts: Because its metabolism saturates within the therapeutic range, small dose increases can cause disproportionately large rises in phenytoin levels.
Phenytoin is a strong inducer of CYP3A4 and other enzymes, reducing the effectiveness of many drugs including hormonal contraceptives.
